newsitem.title: LEBANON: Optimism over poll boosts Beirut stocks, SOLIDERE.
newsitem.headline: Optimism over poll boosts Beirut stocks, SOLIDERE.

text.p: Shares on Beirut's secondary market rallied in the week ending on Friday on the back of Lebanon's biggest company SOLIDERE and boosted by investor optimism over Lebanon's current parliamentary elections.

"It reflects the optimism of investors regarding the outcome of the four rounds of elections so far and the economic implications of these results," said Alain Balian, deputy manager for structured and corporate finance at Lebanon Invest.

Dealers said momentum on the secondary market (BSM) and the official bourse was building thanks to the election victory of billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and many of his supporters, which increased confidence in the Lebanese economy.
The final round of elections takes place on Sunday in the eastern Bekaa valley. Pro-government candidates scored an overwhelming victory in the first four rounds.
Both A and B shares in SOLIDERE, the real estate company rebuilding the war-ravaged city centre of Beirut, soared in an overall upbeat market.
A shares -- distributed to former holders of property rights in the Beirut central district -- rose 3.1 percent on the privately-operated BSM to $108.5 from $105.25 last Friday.
B shares -- issued in a $650-million subscription in January 1994 -- rose 4.6 percent to $111.375 from last Friday's close of $106.5.

On the official Beirut Stock Exchange, prices of cement company Ciments Libanais rose to $1.375 from $1.25 last week. Industrial piping manufacturer Eternit closed virtually unchanged at $1.9375 from $1.938 on July 15 when it was last traded.

The Lebanon Invest Share Price Index (LISPI) rose 2.46 percent on the week to 84.27 and the BLOM Stock Index (BSI) rose 4.37 percent to 951.81. The two indices cover both the secondary and official stock markets.
"This is the highest increase in the LISPI since it was launched in January," Lebanon Invest's Balian said.

Total weekly turnover on the Beirut Stock Exchange was 8,700 shares. There was no trade throughout the week in Ciments Blancs' and shares or Uniceramic's. Weekly turnover on the BSM rose to 43,995 shares from 40,104 last week with trade valued at $4,692,973 against $4,238,562.

SOLIDERE, the backbone of Lebanon stock trading, is due to move its shares from the BSM to the official bourse on September 30, adding some $2 billion to the BSE's capitalisation, currently calculated at less than $400 million.
"The market is moving higher driven by price increases. I expect this momentum to develop. This in turn should encourage more companies to list on the Beirut Stock Exchange," a dealer told Reuters.

SOLIDERE declined to comment on Friday on market rumours in Beirut that it was preparing to offer Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) on the international market worth up to $100 million. -- Zeina Soufan, Beirut editorial (9611) 645456 353078 861723
